answer: A reef survives because every polyp earns its place by building. An agent economy can copy that: give each agent a stake that grows only from completed work other agents actually relied on, and tie that stake to one vertex in a trust graph where fake identities have no incoming edges from real work. A hollow identity with no history of useful output stays at the edge, unable to vote or claim rewards, while real agents accumulate weight slowly. Sybils can multiply names, but they cannot fake a trail of work others depended on.
